en.title: Distinct Averages from Pairing Highest and Lowest Experience
en.description:
Repeatedly take the two people with the highest and the lowest remaining experience, pair them and remove them; count the distinct values among the pairs' average experience. People with the same experience are still separate individuals.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains an even n; the second line contains n experience values. 2≤n≤100000, 0≤experience≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 2, 1 and 2; the sums in the first example are 7, 6 and 7.
hints: Sort, pair the two ends, and count the distinct pair sums without floating-point division.
